newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Australia, Indonesia discuss Timor gap oil.
newsitem.headline: Australia, Indonesia discuss Timor gap oil.

text.p: Australian and Indonesian energy ministers on Thursday discussed developments on oil exploration in the Timor Gap and hoped it would enter the production stage.
Australian Resouces and Energy Minister Warwick Parer said he held talks with his Indonesian counterpart Ida Bagus Sudjana that also touched on the good ties between the two nations.
"We had very good discussions. (A) very cooperative relationship exists between Australia and Indonesia on this zone of cooperation," Parer told Reuters.

Indonesia and Australia signed the Timor Gap Treaty in 1989 to allow them to search for oil and share the exploitation of possbile oil reserves in the 23,550 square mile (61,000 square km) area in the Timor Sea.
The talks were the seventh so far between the two countries on progress in the Timor Gap.

"The seventh meeting of ministers from both countries have discussed the progress in exploration activities and the prospects of oil and gas in the cooperation zone," Indonesia's mines and energy ministry said in a statement.
It said 15 production-sharing contracts involving several companies, including Australia's BHP Petroleum and Woodside Petroleum Ltd have been issued.
Parer said exploration contracts had now been awarded for nearly all of the zone of cooperation in the Timor gap.
"We are hopeful that we are now moving from the exploration stage into the production stage in one or two areas," he said.
He said he hoped the recent gas find by Petroz NL at the Bayu-Undan gas/condensate field in the Gap would lead to production.
"I would imagine that particular gas (find), because of the location, would be an export product," he added.
Petroz has said proven, probable and possible reserves of sales gas, classified as potential liquefied natural gas, total between five and six trillion cubic feet (tcf) in Bayu-Undan.
